{
  "root_cause": "IP address space overlap (overlapping subnets). Both branch offices are using the exact same subnet (192.168.1.0/24), causing routing ambiguity since the router cannot distinguish between local traffic and remote traffic for the same destination network.",
  "confidence": 95,
  "evidence": "Branch A's local Vlan1 interface is configured with 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0, yet the routing table shows 192.168.1.0/24 is also routed via the WAN link Se0/0/0, creating a conflict where the router has overlapping paths for the same subnet.",
  "next_command": "show ip route",
  "fix_steps": [
    "Re-address one of the branch networks to use a unique non-overlapping private subnet (e.g., 192.168.2.0/24).",
    "Alternatively, implement Network Address Translation (NAT) on the WAN routers to translate the overlapping addresses if re-addressing is not immediately possible.",
    "Update static routes or routing protocols accordingly to reflect the new unique subnet paths."
  ]
}

parsed.root_cause: IP address space overlap (overlapping subnets). Both branch offices are using the exact same subnet (192.168.1.0/24), causing routing ambiguity since the router cannot distinguish between local traffic and remote traffic for the same destination network.
parsed.evidence: Branch A's local Vlan1 interface is configured with 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0, yet the routing table shows 192.168.1.0/24 is also routed via the WAN link Se0/0/0, creating a conflict where the router has overlapping paths for the same subnet.
fix_steps: Re-address one of the branch networks to use a unique non-overlapping private subnet (e.g., 192.168.2.0/24).
Alternatively, implement Network Address Translation (NAT) on the WAN routers to translate the overlapping addresses if re-addressing is not immediately possible.
Update static routes or routing protocols accordingly to reflect the new unique subnet paths.
